title: A hero that costs
subtitle: nothing while it's still.
summary: Fill an astro-base-engine animation slot with a Fizlet scene: lazy, settles to zero frames, keeps the slot's text alternative.
lead: An Astro page engine (astro-base-engine) renders each animation slot on a page as a sized, described placeholder. `@fzlt/core/slot` fills it with a scene that loads only near the viewport, never under reduced motion, and settles to zero frames once nothing moves. The heroes on this site's [home page](/) are built this way.

body.text: The page already has the figure, from the engine's `[slot animation]` block: `<figure class="ae-slot" data-slot-target="home#hero" role="img" aria-label="…">`. Its size, its placeholder and its text alternative are the page's. The scene only adds motion.

blocks.heading: 2. What the slot does for you

items.title: Lazy
items.body: Nothing loads until the slot comes within `margin` (default `"200px"`) of the viewport, and then not before the main thread is idle (`requestIdleCallback`, at most `idle` ms, default 1000).

items.title: The first tap counts
items.body: A tap on the slot before the scene is up loads it at once and reaches `mount` as `first = { x, y, at }`: an intent, not the original pointer event, whose pointer is gone by then.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.body: With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the scene never loads and the placeholder stays. If the setting turns on mid-scene, the scene goes and the placeholder comes back.

items.title: Accessible and contained
items.body: `role="img"` and `aria-label` stay. The scene gets its own stage (`contain: strict`), hidden from assistive tech until the scene returns `accessible: true`. Every change goes through a ledger, so `destroy()` puts the slot back exactly.

body.text: A hero's live chunk has a budget of 10 KB gzip. The page build (kernel, `@fzlt/core/slot`, `@fzlt/core/input`, `@fzlt/core/fx`) is {size:page build (kernel+slot+input+fx)}, so the scene's own code gets about 3 KB. Sound, debug, the pad, the HUD, match and the Board UI never get pulled into it (a test checks).

`settle: 0.5` and `fps: 30` are the two lines that make it cheap: half a second after the last `busy()` the engine asks for no frames at all, and while it plays it asks for 30 a second, not one per vsync.

seo.title: Fill an Astro animation slot with a Fizlet scene
